method: The listed basmati rice quantity is the dry, uncooked weight. Follow the cooking and assembly steps below for this measured portion.

Start the 70g dry basmati rice first: this is the uncooked weight. Use the water quantity and cooking time on the rice packet; simmer until tender, then drain if the packet method requires it. Keep covered briefly while finishing the pan, then serve immediately.
Wash and drain the 100g spinach. Use 160g peeled raw king prawns. Fully defrost frozen prawns in the fridge and drain before cooking. Keep them separate from the prepared vegetables.

Warm a non-stick frying pan over a medium-low heat; this recipe does not include frying oil. Add the raw king prawns in one layer and cook for 3–5 minutes, turning, until every prawn is pink outside and opaque in the centre with no translucent flesh. Transfer to a clean plate; keep the pan for the vegetables. Never reuse the plate or utensils that held the raw food without washing them.

Put the 120g chopped tomatoes and 25g medium curry paste into the same frying pan. Stir over a medium-low heat, then cover and simmer gently for 5 minutes. Stir twice; keep the heat low enough that the tomato liquid does not boil dry.
Add the washed spinach in two handfuls, cover for 1 minute, then stir. Cook for another 2–3 minutes until wilted throughout.

Return the cooked prawns at the end and heat for 1 minute until the whole dish is steaming hot; do not simmer them through the longer vegetable cooking stage. Spoon over the freshly cooked rice and serve immediately.

review.notes: Opaque prawns with wilted spinach and tomato curry over white long-grain basmati; no invented coconut cream or garnish.
review.alt: Prawn and spinach curry with basmati rice
